question: Which of the following hydrocarbons generally produces a clean flame?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ethane is a saturated hydrocarbon, also known as an alkane, with the chemical formula C₂H₆.
 
• It burns with a clean, blue flame, producing carbon dioxide and water, indicating complete combustion.
 
• Alkanes like ethane typically produce clean flames because they have a higher hydrogen-to-carbon ratio compared to unsaturated hydrocarbons.
 
• Ethane's clean combustion makes it a preferred fuel in domestic and industrial applications where soot production needs to be minimized.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Combustion of Hydrocarbons**:

 
 
• Combustion is a chemical process in which a substance reacts with oxygen to give off heat.
 
• Complete combustion of hydrocarbons typically produces carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water (H₂O).
 
• Incomplete combustion can produce carbon monoxide (CO) and soot (carbon particles).
 
 
 
• **Types of Hydrocarbons**:
 
 
• **Alkanes**: Saturated hydrocarbons with single bonds only (e.g., methane, ethane).
 
• **Alkenes**: Unsaturated hydrocarbons with at least one double bond (e.g., ethylene).
 
• **Alkynes**: Unsaturated hydrocarbons with at least one triple bond (e.g., acetylene).
 
 
 
• **Flame Types**:
 
 
• **Blue Flame**: Indicates complete combustion with sufficient oxygen, producing less soot.
 
• **Yellow Flame**: Indicates incomplete combustion, often producing soot.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Ethane**:
 
 
• Ethane is used as a petrochemical feedstock to produce ethylene through steam cracking.
 
• It is also used in refrigeration systems and as an industrial gas.
